name: The Royal Hawaiian
positioning: Historic pink beachfront resort on Waikiki Beach, opened in 1927 on the grounds of the Summer Palace of Hawaiian royalty (officially The Royal Hawaiian, a Luxury Collection Resort, Waikiki)
best_for: Travelers who want Hawaiian history and heritage right on Waikiki Beach
Guests who want an ocean-view room with a private balcony in the Mailani Tower
Travelers interested in Hawaiian cultural activities and ceremonies

facts.text: The hotel has distinctive Moorish-style architecture and is painted pink.
The resort sits on the grounds of the Summer Palace of Hawaiian royalty.
During World War II, the US Navy leased the hotel as a rest and relaxation center for Navy personnel.
The Royal Hawaiian is a member of Historic Hotels of America.
Historic Wing rooms have custom carved doors, polished wood accents and bespoke pink-hued wallpaper.
The hotel has direct access to Waikiki Beach.
The Waikiki Beach Boys guide guests on surfing lessons, outrigger canoe surfing and stand-up paddle boarding.
Cultural activities include making floral leis and lauhala bracelets and playing the ukulele, with a different activity each day.
The Ahaaina Luau is held on Mondays and Thursdays on the Ocean Lawn.
The Mai Tai first found a home in Hawaii at The Royal Hawaiian.
International Marketplace Waikiki and The Royal Hawaiian Shopping Center are a 5-minute walk from the hotel.

highlights.text: The hotel is known as the Pink Palace of the Pacific.
Every room in the Mailani Tower has ocean views and a private balcony.
Malulani Pool is reserved exclusively for hotel guests, with loungers under pink umbrellas.
Abhasa Spa offers spa garden treatments in a tropical cabana setting.
Hiuwai is a traditional sunrise ceremony by the water representing purification and cleansing.

considerations.text: Guest rooms, historic suites and resort spaces are being revitalized ahead of the resort's centennial.
Condé Nast Traveler notes Historic Wing rooms are smaller, and some feel a little dated.
Condé Nast Traveler notes beach chairs, umbrellas, parking and resort fees can add up quickly.
